title: Output to Outcome, Ch 0: When AI Removes the Bottleneck: From Outputs to Outcomes
description: Episode 1 of our book-club series on Mik Kersten's "Output to Outcome: An Operating Model for the Age of AI" (IT Revolution, 2026). Chapter 0, "Foundations," comes after the Preface, Prompt and Introduction and before Part I's three models: the Product Operating Model, the Outcome Loop and the Outcome Tree. Kersten argues that AI is making knowledge output nearly free, which moves the bottleneck from producing work to the organization itself. We cover the productivity paradox, the Theory of Constraints (and the car-plant paint shop), the earlier shift to software as a service, Carlota Perez's model of technological revolutions and her "golden age," the "three million Shakespeare plays" problem, and Kersten's account of Cognition's weekly outcome loop, where it throws away much of its code. We also cover the risk he warns about: AI's gains piling up in a few giants. Built from an IntuiBloom knowledge graph. title: Output to Outcome, Ch 1: AI Won't Fix Your Company If the Bottleneck Isn't Code
description: Episode 2 of our book-club series on Mik Kersten's "Output to Outcome: An Operating Model for the Age of AI" (IT Revolution, 2026). Chapter 1, "Product Operating Model," opens Part I, "Outcome Management," and is the first of the book's three foundational models, before the Outcome Loop (Ch 2) and the Outcome Tree (Ch 3). Kersten argues that AI's tenfold boost to coding won't help companies whose bottleneck sits elsewhere. In his State of the Industry data, only 8% of the time from idea to running software went to building it. We cover the Theory of Constraints and the jammed on-ramp, the history from McCallum's org chart to Gantt charts, Snowden's Cynefin framework and when to run a project versus a product, irreducible uncertainty and where AI can augment but not replace decisions, Reinertsen's life cycle profitability, the operating-model dysfunctions in Kersten's reports, and Commonwealth Bank of Australia's path from project to product to AI-native engineering. Built from an IntuiBloom knowledge graph. Explore the IntuiBloom graph: https://www.IntuiBloom.com/share/AL1vJA_m_BgKI2qgGiDOYX0qCm-QLrCkQtXXUnDLVzY=

title: Output to Outcome, Ch 2: The Outcome Loop: Constraints, AI Surplus, and the Next Bottleneck
description: Episode 3 of our book-club series on Mik Kersten's "Output to Outcome: An Operating Model for the Age of AI" (IT Revolution, 2026). Chapter 2, "The Outcome Loop," sits in the middle of Part I, "Outcome Management." It builds on Chapter 1's Product Operating Model, sets up Chapter 3's Outcome Tree, and is the core model that the book's seven shifts in Part II build on. Kersten defines the loop as the feedback system that connects inputs (strategy and budget) to outputs (activities and artifacts) to outcomes (employee, customer and business) and back again. We cover production elasticity and Amazon, the lineage from outcome-based healthcare and Jobs to Be Done to OKRs, Kersten's own path from PhD research to Tasktop, key results versus KPIs, the TeenWellness worked example, why the loop is a hypothesis test, broken telemetry and the "counting procedures" trap, applying the Theory of Constraints, and how the VS Code team's bottleneck moved from delivery to onboarding to code review as AI took over more of the output. Built from an IntuiBloom knowledge graph. Explore the IntuiBloom graph: https://www.IntuiBloom.com/share/gCUMm1v5ojOoiE32udczXYQRC4iQinUtoSavvxJygLM=
